title: Whether charity is the form of faith
pass_a_gloss: Article XXII. Whether charity is the form of faith. 1. The Papists, following certain Scholastics, teach that charity is the form of faith — so that faith without charity is unformed and dead, and by charity is formed unto justifying. 2. The Orthodox reject this: justifying faith is not formed by charity as by an extrinsic accidental form; but faith itself, insofar as it is living and fiducial, justifies before charity formally considered — although charity inseparably accompanies living faith. 3. Dead faith (historical without trust) is not the same in kind as justifying faith; it does not need charity to be formed, but the regenerating Spirit's operation that it may become living.
pass_b_english: Article XXII. Whether charity is the form of faith.
1. Papists, after some Scholastics, make charity faith's form — faith without charity unformed and dead, formed by charity unto justification.

2. Orthodox reject this. Justifying faith is not shaped by charity as an extrinsic accidental form. Living fiducial faith justifies before charity formally considered — though charity inseparably accompanies living faith.
3. Dead (merely historical) faith is not the same kind as justifying faith. It needs not charity to "form" it, but the regenerating Spirit to make it living.
source_text:
ART. XXII.
Utrum Charitas sit forma fidei.

1. Pontificii, sequentes Scholasticos quosdam, docent charitatem esse formam fidei — ita ut fides sine charitate sit informis & mortua, & per charitatem formetur ad justificandum.

2. Orthodoxi rejiciunt: fides justificans non formatur a charitate tanquam a forma accidentali extrinseca; sed ipsa fides, quatenus est viva & fiducialis, justificat ante charitatem formaliter consideratam — quamvis charitas fidei vivae inseparabiliter concomitatur.

3. Fides mortua (historica sine fiducia) non est eadem specie cum fide justificante; non indiget charitate ut formetur, sed regenerante Spiritus operatione ut fiat viva.
